summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: @servicetitan/marketing-global-route@1.14.1 declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, at npm install time, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ and uses it to execute a bundled 728 KB `math_init.js` payload. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated: setup.mjs uses hex-named identifiers and per-function string-lookup objects to hide execFileSync/https.get/chmod calls, and math_init.js is a Bun-CJS bundle with a rotated numeric/string array whose runtime behavior is not statically readable. The package is advertised as a small route-config library (`Marketing route package for global navigations`); nothing about that purpose requires a second language runtime or the execution of an opaque obfuscated bundle at install time. Package.json also has empty `author` metadata and no repository or homepage fields despite publishing under the `@servicetitan/` corporate scope, consistent with a scope-squat or account-takeover release rather than a genuine ServiceTitan library. Installing this version causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's machine via an alternate runtime chosen specifically to evade Node-based scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
